clue.text: Hearty, like some footballers having a drink

parts.note: backs are defensive players in football
lapping is drinking with the tongue, as a cat does

explanation.surface: Defenders out for a pint are full of jovial cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearty' looks like a description of the footballers, but it is the definition: hearty in the sense of effusively friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: Effusive, back-thumping camaraderie is a hearty manner, so the adjective fits a jovial greeting.

clue.text: Fish identified by student in straw hat

indicators.note: the student letter goes in, placed inside the word for the hat

parts.note: a boater is a flat-topped straw hat
L for learner, as on a learner driver's plate, stands for a student

explanation.surface: A fish is recognised by the student wearing a straw hat.
explanation.walkthrough: A BLOATER is a smoked herring, a traditional British breakfast fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A cured herring is a kind of fish, so the general word defines it.

clue.text: Mild saint

definitions.meaning: gentle or merciful in temper, or pleasant in weather
a holy person canonised by the Church, here one particular name

explanation.definitionFit: Clement weather is gentle and mild; Clement was the name of several early saints and popes, such as St Clement of Rome.

clue.text: Gin — doubles for a start — with rum: it takes some beating!

parts.note: a gin is a trap for catching animals, the same as a snare

indicators.note: for a start means only the opening letter of the word doubles is wanted

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A gin, then doubles, then rum: a drinking session that is hard to beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' and 'rum' look like drinks; gin is really the trapping device. 'it takes some beating!' is the playful definition: a drum is beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A drum with rattling wires is struck with sticks in performance, so it is literally beaten.

clue.text: Scope for players leaving 25

indicators.note: leaving means the players depart from the other entry's word, taking their letters away

parts.note: the answer to 25 across, meaning surrounding
E and N, East and North, are two of the four players at a bridge table

explanation.surface: There is room for the performers to leave clue 25.
explanation.walkthrough: 'players' looks like actors; in crosswords the four bridge players are N, E, S, W, and here East and North depart.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambit means the range or extent of something, which is its scope.

clue.text: Repton's unusually small private entrance

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of the school's name are arranged in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Repton, an English public school, has an unusually small back gate.
explanation.walkthrough: Repton is an English boarding school; the possessive 's supplies its S as a letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: A postern is a back or side gate, typically small and unobtrusive, in a castle or city wall.

clue.text: Perplex by using common sense about odd characters in Nepal

indicators.note: about means the word for common sense goes around the other letters

parts.note: nous is practical common sense

indicators.note: the odd characters are the first, third and fifth letters of the word Nepal

explanation.surface: Puzzle someone by using practical wisdom about strange folk in Nepal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd characters' suggests strange people; it means the odd-numbered letters N, P, L, which go inside NOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: To nonplus someone is to baffle them so they do not know how to respond.

clue.text: Bill holds up the course? What a bloomer!

indicators.note: in a down entry the name for Bill sits underneath, holding the course up above it

parts.note: a sweet is the dessert course of a meal
Bill is a short form of the name William

explanation.surface: Someone called Bill delays the next part of the race, which is quite a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder; it is a flowering plant. Sweet William is a garden flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that produces blooms is a bloomer, and this cottage-garden flower is one.

clue.text: Try to persuade gunners to enclose state rocket range

parts.note: to woo is to try to win someone over
ME is the postal abbreviation for Maine, a US state
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners of the British Army

explanation.surface: Artillerymen are coaxed into fencing off an area of land for missile testing.
explanation.walkthrough: WOOMERA is the rocket and weapons test range in South Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: This South Australian site is a weapons testing ground used for launching missiles.

clue.text: Dog's bed I observed around New Jersey

indicators.note: around signals the bed and I placed around the abbreviation for the state

parts.note: a base is the bed or foundation something rests on

explanation.surface: A dog's basket, I noticed, was placed near New Jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'observed' is just a link word: 'I observed' is the setter's aside. The basenji is a barkless African hunting dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The basenji is a breed of hound from central Africa, so the general word covers it.

clue.text: Make speech supporting worker, say, outside quiet policeman's office

indicators.note: in a down entry the speech word sits below, supporting what comes above
outside means the worker word goes around the letter for quiet

parts.note: a worker ant or bee is an example of an insect
P, for piano, is the musical direction meaning quiet
to orate is to deliver a formal speech

explanation.surface: Give a talk backing a labourer outside a silent police station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worker' looks like a labourer; ', say' shows it is one example of a broader word, the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspectorate is the body or post of an inspector, a senior police rank.

clue.text: The ultimate tin-opener adopted by old-time engineers

indicators.note: adopted by means the opening letter is taken in by the engineers' letters

parts.note: ex- means former, from an old time
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers of the British Army

indicators.note: the opener of tin is its first letter

explanation.surface: The best can-opener ever was taken up by old army engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tin-opener' looks like a kitchen gadget, but it means only the letter that opens 'tin'. REME is a British Army corps, so 'old-time engineers' are ex-REME.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme means the farthest or utmost degree, the ultimate point.

clue.text: A supporter of horticultural training

parts.note: reads like a backer of gardening courses, but describes a lattice frame that holds up climbing plants and guides how they grow

explanation.definitionFit: A garden lattice props up climbers, and gardeners train plants along it.

clue.text: Best yarn the press chief rejected

annotationWithheld.why: Best yarn the press chief rejected (5) for WORST: WORSTED (yarn) less ED (the press chief, editor); the only parse has 'the press chief' as one leaf giving ED, which the check refuses as a first-letter pick (selectorAsCut) though ED is the editor, not a pick
annotationWithheld.clue: Best yarn the press chief rejected

clue.text: Talk nostalgically about daring skirts before the church put a stop to them

indicators.note: before means the skirts come ahead of the church letters

parts.note: re means about or concerning
minis are short, daring skirts
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Recalling the old days of short skirts until the Church banned them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put a stop to them' adds surface colour and shows the church letters coming at the very end.
explanation.definitionFit: To reminisce is to recall past times fondly, chatting about the good old days.

clue.text: Treatise on motion of, moon, accompanied by diagram

indicators.note: motion of signals that the letters of moon are moved about

parts.note: a graph is a diagram plotting values

explanation.surface: A scholarly paper on how the moon moves, with a chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word here, joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A monograph is a detailed scholarly study of one subject, a kind of treatise.

clue.text: Many a true scholar in fashionable City company

annotationWithheld.why: Many a true scholar in fashionable City company (9) for LIVERYMAN: L (many) + I (a) + VERY (true) + MA (scholar) leaves the final N unaccounted for, and no parse found uses every word
annotationWithheld.clue: Many a true scholar in fashionable City company

clue.text: Sell one small fish

parts.note: to vend is to sell
an ace counts as one in cards

explanation.surface: Sell a single little fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The vendace is a small whitefish found in a few British and Scandinavian lakes.

clue.text: Telephoned about family's status

indicators.note: about means the word for telephoned goes around the family word

parts.note: rang means telephoned
kin are one's family or relatives

explanation.surface: Someone phoned to ask about the family's social standing.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranking is a position on a scale, one's standing or status.

clue.text: Mac in a cravat

parts.note: Mac, the common prefix of Scottish surnames, stands for a Scotsman

explanation.surface: A Scotsman wearing a neckerchief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mac' looks like a raincoat; it is a Scot. An ascot is a broad neck scarf, named after the racecourse at Ascot.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascot is a wide neck scarf worn looped under the chin, a type of cravat.

clue.text: Still amicable, perhaps, after losing head

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the remaining letters could be arranged some other way
losing head means the first letter of amicable is dropped

explanation.surface: Still friendly, perhaps, after being beheaded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb meaning yet; it is a distilling apparatus.
explanation.definitionFit: An alembic is an old distilling apparatus, and a still is equipment for distilling spirits.

clue.text: Clot's sudden dismissal over a pound

indicators.note: in a down entry over means the dismissal sits on top of what follows

parts.note: conge is an abrupt dismissal, from French
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: An idiot is fired abruptly over a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clot' looks like a fool; it is the verb, to thicken. The 's is a link (Clot is ...).
explanation.definitionFit: To congeal is to thicken from liquid into a solid mass, just as blood clots.

clue.text: Game portion supplied in lodging-house in Gilbert and Sullivan

parts.note: an inn is a house offering lodging
G is the initial of W S Gilbert, the comic opera librettist
S is the initial of Arthur Sullivan, the composer

explanation.surface: A share of the game is served in a boarding house in a comic opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Gilbert and Sullivan wrote Victorian comic operas; their initials give G and S. An innings is a team's turn to bat in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a side's batting turn is one division of the match, a portion of the game.

clue.text: Slur Theocritus first disposed of in one of his letters

indicators.note: disposed of means the poet's opening letter is thrown out of the slur word

parts.note: a stigma is a mark of disgrace, a slur

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the name Theocritus

explanation.surface: Theocritus first got rid of an insult in one of his letters.
explanation.walkthrough: Theocritus was an ancient Greek poet, so 'his letters' are Greek letters, not correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, which a Greek poet would write in.

clue.text: There's delight about a new King, he gathers

indicators.note: about means the delight word goes around the following letters

parts.note: glee is delight
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: There is joy surrounding a new monarch as he gathers his people.
explanation.walkthrough: A gleaner gathers leftover grain from a harvested field.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who collects leftovers from a field after harvest is one who gathers.

clue.text: Conveying home an ingenious container

indicators.note: container says the phrase home an ingenious holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Bringing home a clever box.
explanation.walkthrough: 'container' looks like a box being carried home; it is the signal that the answer sits inside the words.
explanation.definitionFit: A meaning look is one that conveys or expresses something, so the adjective fits.

clue.text: Surrounding a doctor? That's not tolerated initially

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's qualification
i.e. is short for id est, that is

indicators.note: initially means take the first letters of not and tolerated

explanation.surface: Encircling a physician: is that not allowed?
explanation.definitionFit: Ambient describes the environment all around, such as ambient noise or temperature.

clue.text: Man with an old paper title to nearly all of the land

parts.note: Geo. is the abbreviation for George, a man's name
The Graphic was a Victorian illustrated weekly newspaper

indicators.note: nearly means the word all is cut short by its final letter

explanation.surface: A man holding the title to an old newspaper owns almost the whole territory.
explanation.walkthrough: The Graphic was a well-known British illustrated newspaper (1869-1932).
explanation.definitionFit: Geographical relates to the physical features of the earth, describing matters of the land.
